```{r}
library(tmap)
```

An interactive map lets the reader explore the data: zoom in, click on features for details, and switch between layers. In tmap, the same code makes a static or an interactive map; only the mode differs (see the article on [modes](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap/articles/basics_modes)). This example shows the features that make an interactive map useful.

```{r}
tmap_mode("view")
```

## A first map

A choropleth of the Happy Planet Index, with the default basemaps:

```{r}
tm_shape(World) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "HPI", fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "pu_gn"))
```

Hover over a country to see its name, and click on it to see the values. The layer control at the top left switches between the basemaps.

## Popups, groups, and basemaps

The next map adds:

* **popups** with `tm_popup()`: which variables are shown, with which labels and number format;
* a **second map variable**: life expectancy. The two choropleths are in separate layer groups. With `group.control = "radio"`, only one of them is shown at a time;
* **metropolitan areas**, as bubbles with labels, in a third group that can be switched on and off. Labels that overlap are hidden, in the order of `priority`, and appear when zooming in;
* a single basemap (with several basemaps, these would also be radio buttons), and a **minimap**.

```{r}
tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
tm_shape(World) +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "HPI",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "pu_gn"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend("Happy Planet Index"),
    fill_alpha = 0.8,
    id = "name",
    popup = tm_popup(
      vars = c("Happy Planet Index" = "HPI", "Life expectancy" = "life_exp",
               "Well-being" = "well_being", "Ecological footprint" = "footprint"),
      format = tm_label_format(digits = 1)),
    group = "Happy Planet Index", group.control = "radio") +
  tm_polygons(
    fill = "life_exp",
    fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.blues"),
    fill.legend = tm_legend("Life expectancy"),
    fill_alpha = 0.8,
    id = "name",
    group = "Life expectancy", group.control = "radio") +
tm_shape(metro) +
  tm_bubbles(
    size = "pop2020",
    size.scale = tm_scale_continuous_area(),
    size.legend = tm_legend("Population 2020"),
    fill = "gold", col = "grey30",
    id = "name",
    popup = tm_popup(vars = c("Population 2020" = "pop2020", "Population 1990" = "pop1990")),
    group = "Metropolitan areas") +
  tm_labels("name", priority = "pop2020", group = "Metropolitan areas") +
tm_minimap()
```

The `id` is the name that is shown when hovering over a feature, and the title of the popup. See the article on [layer groups](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap/articles/adv_groups) for more about groups, e.g. to show layers only at certain zoom levels.

## Other interactive modes

The extension package [**tmap.mapgl**](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap/articles/ext_mapgl) adds the modes `"maplibre"` and `"mapbox"`, which use vector graphics and WebGL. They are faster for large data, and support 3D polygons and other projections. The code above also works in these modes:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(tmap.mapgl)
tmap_mode("maplibre")
```

## Sharing the map

An interactive map is saved as a stand-alone HTML file with `tmap_save()`, which can be shared or put on a website:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
map = tm_shape(World) + tm_polygons("HPI")
tmap_save(map, "world_hpi.html")
```

In **shiny** apps, interactive maps are made with `renderTmap()` and `tmapOutput()` (see the article on [shiny integration](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap/articles/adv_shiny)).

```{r, include = FALSE}
tmap_mode("plot")
```
